The Army Commanders’ Conference, the Indian Army’s apex-level biannual forum, commenced in New Delhi on Wednesday (October 21, 2026), with senior military leadership set to deliberate on the evolving security environment, operational preparedness and capability development. The conference, chaired by the Chief of the Army Staff (COAS), is being held from October 21 to 23.
According to the Ministry of Defence, a key highlight will be the release of the Land Warfare Doctrine by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The doctrine is expected to provide an overarching framework to prepare the Army for the changing character of warfare and future conflicts.
Mr. Singh will address the conference, while the Chief of Defence Staff, Chief of the Naval Staff, and Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology will deliver talks on contemporary security-related issues.
The Defence Minister will also unveil the annual United Nations Journal and felicitate Army personnel who have made notable contributions while serving as United Nations peacekeepers. The recognition will honour their professionalism and service towards international peace and security under the UN banner.
As part of the conference, the Army Chief will confer awards for Green Military Stations and Aviation Flight Safety recognising excellence in environmental sustainability, resource management and the promotion of a strong aviation safety culture.
The three-day conference will provide a platform for the Army’s senior leadership to review ongoing initiatives, identify future priorities, and formulate policy directions to build a technologically enabled, adaptive and future-ready force.
The deliberations come amid an evolving security environment that requires continued attention to operational readiness, modernisation, and the integration of emerging technologies into military capabilities.
